response_text: Without having reviewed the underlying studies directly, a generic expectation based on general familiarity with this research area would suggest a mixed but somewhat majority-leaning picture: much of the literature likely reports that antioxidant supplementation (vitamin C and/or E) has no significant effect on exercise training adaptations under many conditions, though a meaningful minority of findings probably indicate blunting effects, particularly with high-dose or chronic supplementation during endurance training where reactive oxygen species signaling is thought to be important for mitochondrial biogenesis and adaptive responses. Enhancement effects would generally be expected to be rare or limited to specific contexts, such as protecting against excessive oxidative stress or muscle damage in unaccustomed or high-intensity exercise.
